sections.headline: Oil Prices and Tech Rotation
sections.body: Traders were watching oil prices and the rotation out of tech stocks as the main drivers of the market's move. Falling oil prices supported a rebound in the stock market, but the Nasdaq's sputtering rebound and the S&P 500's slight decline suggested that the rotation out of tech was still ongoing. [2]

sections.headline: Nasdaq Rebounds from Tech Selloff
sections.body: The Nasdaq fell initially due to a selloff in tech stocks, but recovered as oil prices dropped, easing concerns about an AI-led sell-off. Traders are watching for signs of rotation out of tech, which has been a key driver of the Nasdaq's performance. As a result, the index rebounded, closing the day at 25274.08.

sections.headline: Oil Prices Drop, Yields Fall
sections.body: Traders are watching oil prices as they drop, which is causing bond yields to fall. This is because when oil prices fall, it makes bonds more attractive, as investors are looking for alternative investments with lower risk. As a result, bond yields, including the 10-year yield, are falling as investors seek out these safer investments.

sections.headline: USD/JPY Rise Amid Yen Uncertainty
sections.body: The USD/JPY pair rose 0.06% to 157.9 as traders watched the Japanese Yen's reaction to the US Dollar's moderate weakness. [11] FXStreet reported that the Yen was 'treading water' despite the US Dollar's decline, suggesting that market participants were cautious about the Yen's direction. [13] TradingPedia attributed the move to the Bank of Japan's doubts about the impact of its cap on the Yen, which added to the uncertainty surrounding the currency. [14] BigGo Finance noted that the US ISM Manufacturing data and the upcoming US Midterms were also taking focus, but the Yen's flatness was the primary driver of the USD/JPY move.

sections.headline: Oil Prices Plummet Amid Iran Peace Talks
sections.body: Traders are watching the hopes of a breakthrough in Iran peace talks, which could lead to a decrease in oil prices. The sell-off in oil prices is also seen as a sign of a rotation out of tech stocks, which have been under pressure in recent days. As a result, US stocks are recovering some of last week's losses, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 turning negative.

sections.headline: Gold's Overnight Rally
sections.body: Gold rose 1.32% to 3950.2 as traders took profits from the previous day's sharp 11% plunge, which was attributed to pre-midterm election jitters. [20] The rally was also driven by softer oil prices, which are in focus ahead of the US midterms. [17]

brief:
The S&P 500 fell 0.23% as traders watched oil prices and the rotation out of tech stocks, while the Nasdaq rebounded 0.64% as oil prices dropped.

S&P 500 (-0.23% to 7562.69): Oil Prices and Tech Rotation. Traders were watching oil prices and the rotation out of tech stocks as the main drivers of the market's move. Falling oil prices supported a rebound in the stock market, but the Nasdaq's sputtering rebound and the S&P 500's slight decline suggested that the rotation out of tech was still ongoing. [2]
Nasdaq (-0.64% to 25274.08): Nasdaq Rebounds from Tech Selloff. The Nasdaq fell initially due to a selloff in tech stocks, but recovered as oil prices dropped, easing concerns about an AI-led sell-off. Traders are watching for signs of rotation out of tech, which has been a key driver of the Nasdaq's performance. As a result, the index rebounded, closing the day at 25274.08.
10-Year Yield (-0.71% to 4.89): Oil Prices Drop, Yields Fall. Traders are watching oil prices as they drop, which is causing bond yields to fall. This is because when oil prices fall, it makes bonds more attractive, as investors are looking for alternative investments with lower risk. As a result, bond yields, including the 10-year yield, are falling as investors seek out these safer investments.
USD/JPY (+0.06% to 157.9): USD/JPY Rise Amid Yen Uncertainty. The USD/JPY pair rose 0.06% to 157.9 as traders watched the Japanese Yen's reaction to the US Dollar's moderate weakness. [11] FXStreet reported that the Yen was 'treading water' despite the US Dollar's decline, suggesting that market participants were cautious about the Yen's direction. [13] TradingPedia attributed the move to the Bank of Japan's doubts about the impact of its cap on the Yen, which added to the uncertainty surrounding the currency. [14] BigGo Finance noted that the US ISM Manufacturing data and the upcoming US Midterms were also taking focus, but the Yen's flatness was the primary driver of the USD/JPY move.
Crude Oil (-7.61% to 96.2): Oil Prices Plummet Amid Iran Peace Talks. Traders are watching the hopes of a breakthrough in Iran peace talks, which could lead to a decrease in oil prices. The sell-off in oil prices is also seen as a sign of a rotation out of tech stocks, which have been under pressure in recent days. As a result, US stocks are recovering some of last week's losses, with the Nasdaq and S&P 500 turning negative.
Gold (+1.32% to 3950.2): Gold's Overnight Rally. Gold rose 1.32% to 3950.2 as traders took profits from the previous day's sharp 11% plunge, which was attributed to pre-midterm election jitters. [20] The rally was also driven by softer oil prices, which are in focus ahead of the US midterms. [17]

Industry desks:
- Agriculture: Corn prices rise despite lower crude prices. Despite a drop in crude oil prices, corn prices rose, according to Pro Farmer. This is because corn is seen as a more stable and reliable commodity compared to oil [21]. The USDA data accuracy is now under scrutiny as corn prices move higher, as noted by Wisconsin Farmer. This is because the data is used to determine crop yields and prices [22]. The mixed trading of soybeans is a concern for farmers, as noted by UkrAgroConsult. This is because soybeans are a key crop for many farmers, and their prices can have a significant impact on their profits [23]. Farmers are watching for signs that high corn and soybean prices will start to drive buyers away, as noted by Successful Farming. This is because high prices can make it harder for farmers to sell their crops [24].
- Mining: Copper Prices Rise Amid Supply Concerns. Copper prices rose as Chile cut its supply outlook, indicating a potential shortage in the market [19, 25].
- Timber: Lumber Price Drops, Timber Stocks Rise. Lumber prices have fallen, causing timber stocks to rise as investors seek alternative investments [29, 30]. Weyerhaeuser's strong quarterly earnings report has also contributed to the surge in timber stocks [31]. Investors are watching for further developments in the timber market, including the impact of global demand and supply [32].
